Statements carrying `tags: [iog]` — those whose cited sources include an author affiliated with [Input Output Research](https://www.iog.io/papers).

**What the tag claims, and what it does not.** It records that somebody on the author list of a cited paper is affiliated with Input Output. It does *not* say the paper was published, funded or endorsed by them, and it says nothing at all about the statement itself, which is this site's own formalization of an open question the paper left. Where the two come apart — a paper by an IO-affiliated author that IO's own publication list does not carry — the tag is still correct, because it is about the author.

This is a *provenance* tag rather than a subject one: it sits alongside the model, form and category chips rather than among the [19 areas](/open-problems/by-area/index.qmd), which say what a statement is about.
